title: Decisiones y reglas de validación

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only concepts marked USABLE in the effective prior ledger count as learned. PARTIAL, MENTION_ONLY, MISCONCEPTION_RISK and MISSING receive no automatic credit.

roadmap_expectation.T1: Booleanos: comparaciones y pertenencia; truthiness y short-circuit
roadmap_expectation.T2: Control: if/elif/else; guard clauses, anidamiento y ramas alcanzables
roadmap_expectation.T3: Reglas: rangos, listas permitidas y combinaciones; decision tables y match cuando aporta claridad
roadmap_expectation.T4: Verificación: invariantes y ejemplos; mensajes accionables y pruebas de ramas

later_boundaries.S05: function definition, return, parameters, type hints
later_boundaries.S06: lists, tuples, dicts, sets, slicing, unpacking
later_boundaries.S07: string methods and Unicode mental model

adversarial_review.most_likely_beginner_failure: The learner understands the prose definition of a condition but cannot trace most worked examples because functions, return, for loops, list/tuple/dict structures and string methods are still unearned prerequisites.
adversarial_review.suspected_hidden_prerequisite: S04 iteration, S05 functions/return/type hints, S06 collections/unpacking, S07 string methods.
adversarial_review.most_likely_misconception: That an invariant is something the program literally cannot violate, and that NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST has one stable meaning even though the lesson maps it to review in T3-A and reject in T3-B.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: opening definition of guard clause; T2-A; T2-B; T3-A; T3-B; T4-A; T4-B code
confirmed_findings.evidence: S03 defines a guard clause as an if at the start of a function that returns immediately and almost every nontrivial example defines a function, often with return and type annotations. V3 schedules function definition/call/return/parameters/type hints in S05.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S01-S02 USABLE ledger only; function syntax from S01/S02 remains MENTION_ONLY.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: One of S03's promised T2 skills, guard clauses, inherently depends on function/return semantics that the roadmap withholds until S05, and the lesson does not teach that prerequisite before relying on it.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can predict a comparison but cannot explain why return ends the route, why code below it is skipped, or why the function call produces the shown status; guard clauses become a copied shape rather than a control-flow model.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: In S03 teach ordering/exclusivity/dead branches without early return, using top-level status assignments or direct prints. Move guard clauses/early return to S05 when functions and return are taught, or explicitly revise the roadmap if guard clauses must remain in S03.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: T1-B, T2-A, T2-B, T3-A, T3-B, T4-A, T4-B code examples
confirmed_findings.evidence: Worked examples repeatedly use for loops to enumerate cases and outputs before V3 teaches for/range/iteration in S04.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Iteration is used as the presentation mechanism for the very evidence the novice is supposed to inspect, so it is not incidental syntax.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot predict why several rows print or how variables such as s, e, c, ex, val and code change between outputs, making the decision logic harder to isolate.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: For S03 theory, write explicit calls/prints for each case or show a static decision/example table. Introduce loops only in S04.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: opening result-shape paragraph; optional contract; T2-B through T4-B code
confirmed_findings.evidence: The opening callout says collections arrive later, but learner-facing theory uses set literals, dict return values, lists of tuples, nested list/dict examples, indexing such as r["code"] and ex["value"], and a dict-of-examples representation before S06 teaches collections and unpacking.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: No collection model beyond a narrow aliasing preview in S02 that was not creditable as mastery.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Structured result containers become essential to understanding status/code/message and branch tests even though the section explicitly promises not to teach collections yet.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A novice can follow accept/reject/review in prose but lose the result once it becomes {status, code}, cannot explain brackets/indexing, and may conflate the rule being taught with the container syntax carrying it.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Keep S03 core results as simple strings or visually rendered tables. A small set used solely to demonstrate membership may remain with one microdefinition; defer dict/list/tuple protocols and indexing to S06.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: figure S03-guard-order attached to T1-A Comparaciones y el operador in
confirmed_findings.evidence: The figure caption discusses moving a guard and changing classification before guard clauses or branch ordering are introduced in T2.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A visual intended to reduce uncertainty introduces a future control-flow construct before its learner-facing definition.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner sees 'guarda' and ordered branch effects before knowing what a guard is, so the figure cannot perform explanatory work at its current position.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Move S03-guard-order to T2-B after branch order and dead branches are explained; keep T1-A visual-free or use a comparison/membership figure.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Chained comparison is explained as equivalent to two comparisons joined by and before and/or are taught in T1-B.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The explanation uses the next subtopic's operator to explain the current subtopic's first mental model.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A ZERO_TECH learner must infer what and does precisely in order to understand why 18 <= edad <= 65 works.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Say 'equivale a exigir que se cumplan las dos comparaciones; Python evalúa edad una sola vez' and introduce the and syntax in T1-B.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The first truthiness list includes (), [], {}, set(), range(0) and mentions while although collections and loop constructs are scheduled later.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: None, bool, numbers and strings are available; collection and range syntax are not.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The novice must decode five future container syntaxes merely to learn the crucial S03 distinction None vs 0.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: Attention shifts from the business distinction to unexplained punctuation and constructors, increasing the chance that the learner memorizes a falsy list instead of learning the policy distinction.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: In the core paragraph use False, None, numeric zero and empty string. Add one sentence that empty collections are also falsy and will be revisited in S06; omit while/range examples here.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The prose defines short-circuit, but the examples '' or 'default', 0 and 99 and 5 and 99 demonstrate operand return values without making skipped evaluation observable.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Comparisons, truthiness and the just-introduced and/or operators.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The learner can observe the final operand value yet has no evidence that the right-hand expression was not evaluated.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may equate short-circuit with 'and/or return a convenient operand' and fail to predict why a guard like edad is not None and edad >= 18 safely avoids the second comparison when edad is None.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Add one process worked example in which the second expression would fail if evaluated, e.g. edad=None followed by edad is not None and edad >= 18, and narrate why the right side is skipped.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: opening paragraph 4 and T4-A invariant definition
confirmed_findings.evidence: The opening says 'un invariante es una promesa que el programa no puede romper' and gives 'el monto nunca es negativo' as an invariant, while the same section validates raw values that can in fact be negative and rejects them.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: An invariant is a condition required/intended to hold at a specified program or domain boundary; bugs or invalid external inputs can violate it. The current definition sounds like an automatically enforced law of the language.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can conclude that once a statement is called an invariant, invalid values cannot exist, making validation/tests conceptually redundant and obscuring the difference between raw-input constraints and post-validation guarantees.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Define an invariant as 'una condición que declaras que debe cumplirse en una etapa concreta, por ejemplo después de validar; el código y las pruebas detectan cuando no se cumple'. Scope examples explicitly to raw vs accepted data.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: T3-B Tablas de decisión y match/case
confirmed_findings.evidence: A learning outcome promises reading a decision table, but theory never renders an actual table with condition columns/rows and actions. It describes the idea, then jumps to prose arrows and match code, even suggesting a dict of examples.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Ordinary tables are part of ZERO_TECH baseline.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The section names and defines a table without teaching the learner how to read one, check coverage of combinations, or translate one row into a branch.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may think a list of code constants or a dict is the decision table and cannot audit whether all business combinations are represented before coding.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Insert one small learner-visible table before match, e.g. code | meaning | status, including default/unknown. Ask the learner to trace each row into if/elif or match.

confirmed_findings.evidence: T3-A explicitly classifies a region outside the allowlist as review and prints R-FUERA 30 -> review. T3-B then maps the stable code NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST to reject without announcing a policy change, even though it says it is scaling the T3-A motor.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner has just learned that unknown and invalid are distinct and that NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST preserves that distinction.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The same cause code receives two incompatible statuses in consecutive subtopics with no different domain contract to explain the change.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner cannot know whether an unknown catalog value is review or reject and may copy either mapping while believing it is the course's canonical policy.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Keep NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST -> review throughout this synthetic policy, or explicitly introduce a new stricter policy/table with a new context and state that the mapping changed by business decision.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The callout tells learners on versions earlier than 3.10 to implement the table with if/elif even though the course states it uses Python 3.12 and S01's stated outcome is a 3.12+ environment.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Course runtime should already be resolved in S01.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: A compatibility fallback reopens a settled prerequisite and encourages unsupported runtimes without educational need.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A learner on an old Python can conclude the environment is acceptable and continue accumulating behavior/version differences instead of fixing the S01 setup contract.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: State only that match requires the course's Python 3.12 runtime; remove the pre-3.10 fallback from the learner path.

confirmed_findings.evidence: Both validators use isinstance(edad, int) without excluding bool. S02 explicitly taught that bool is a subtype of int and that business integer validators should use isinstance(x, int) and not isinstance(x, bool). Executing the S03 logic confirms True/False pass the int check; validate_edad_msg(True) returns OK.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: S02's bool/int edge case was explicitly discussed locally even though the broader validation pattern remained partial.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: S03 violates the exact edge case its previous lesson warned about, turning booleans into ages.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can submit True as edad and receive accept/OK in T4-B, learning that the validator is type-safe when it is not.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: For domain integer fields where bool is invalid, use if not isinstance(edad, int) or isinstance(edad, bool): BAD_TYPE, and add True/False branch cases.

confirmed_findings.subtopic_or_location: T4-A paragraph 2 versus T4-B paragraph 2 and learning outcome 8
confirmed_findings.evidence: T4-A says the professional minimum is at least one example per decision state, but T4-B correctly says one test per branch and gives four paths (None, wrong type, range, OK). Multiple branches can share the same reject state, so one reject example cannot cover them all.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Basic accept/reject/review states and branch model from S03.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The lesson offers two incompatible minimum coverage contracts; the weaker one can miss an entire branch while appearing to satisfy all three statuses.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: A validator with two reject causes can be tested with only one reject input, leaving the other branch broken while the learner believes the minimum has been met.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Change T4-A to 'at least one example per distinct branch; if several branches share a status, each still needs a case'. Keep accept/reject/review coverage as a secondary check.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The invariant example requires isinstance, strip, isdigit, len, dict/list nesting, indexing, for iteration and a function before the learner can focus on what an invariant means. String methods are formally developed later in S07.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: Basic strings only; method-call syntax remained PARTIAL after S02.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The worked example for specification/invariants is harder than the concept because it bundles several unrelated future constructs.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can copy a nine-digit validator but cannot explain which line represents the invariant versus incidental normalization/container mechanics.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Use a previously learned scalar rule such as edad is None / 0<=edad<=120 to demonstrate invariant, counterexample and branch tests. Defer string-method validation to S07.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The text says stable codes allow metrics and i18n later, but i18n has never been introduced and is not needed to understand actionable messages.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: An abbreviation with no learner value at this point creates an external-knowledge obligation.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner may stop to infer or search for i18n while the actual concept is simply that stable codes can later support translated messages.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Replace i18n with 'traducciones de mensajes' or add 'i18n (internacionalización)' if the abbreviation must be preserved.

confirmed_findings.evidence: The lesson says an allowlist is safer than a denylist because forgotten values remain outside, stated as a broad rule before later acknowledging stale/unknown catalog values may require review.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: Fail-closed behavior for a known closed catalog is useful, but 'more secure' is context-dependent and can become operationally wrong when the catalog is incomplete or the policy should review unknown values rather than reject them.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can generalize 'allowlist always safer' to domains where a stale list silently blocks legitimate values or where unknown values require a different state.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: Scope the claim: 'En un catálogo cerrado, una allowlist falla cerrado: lo no enumerado no se acepta automáticamente; según la política puede ir a review o reject.'

confirmed_findings.evidence: CP-N1-A and CASO-LIM-003 remain learner-facing identifiers without a fresh plain-language expansion. S01/S02 audits already marked the CP/CASO family as unresolved for the zero-tech learner.
confirmed_findings.expected_prior_knowledge: The learner knows there is an accumulating project idea, but the internal IDs were not credited as usable terminology.
confirmed_findings.actual_problem: The lesson still treats internal curriculum labels as meaningful nouns instead of explaining the artifact/case they denote.
confirmed_findings.learner_failure_mode: The learner can again wonder whether CASO-LIM-003 is a file/tool and what CP-N1-A specifically means in this section.
confirmed_findings.minimal_fix: At first use write 'CP-N1-A, el proyecto acumulativo de captura y calidad de datos del Nivel 1' and 'CASO-LIM-003, el caso sintético de reglas de esta sección'.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Truthiness explanation is technically wrong because and/or do not always return bool.
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson explicitly states that and/or return an operand and that not returns a boolean; this matches Python's documented semantics.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The chained comparison claim 18 <= edad <= 65 is incorrect.
rejected_findings.reason: Python documents chained comparisons as equivalent in truth conditions to two comparisons joined by and, with the middle expression evaluated once. The placement of and is a sequencing issue, not a technical-error issue.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Membership in a dict checks values, so the lesson's statement about keys is wrong.
rejected_findings.reason: Python's mapping membership semantics do consider keys. The issue is premature collection breadth, not correctness.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: Using is None is incorrect or unnecessarily strict.
rejected_findings.reason: The identity check for the None singleton is canonical and directly supports the lesson's missing-vs-zero distinction.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: match/case is being described as a pure switch and therefore technically false.
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson explicitly calls cases patterns, names OR patterns and wildcard _, and scopes the example to literal finite states. It does not need the full structural-pattern-matching model here.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The first matching case statement claim is false.
rejected_findings.reason: For the unguarded literal patterns shown, the first matching case is selected and later cases are not executed; this matches the language reference.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The warning that assert can be disabled under python -O is false.
rejected_findings.reason: The warning is technically sound and appropriately prevents assert from being presented as production input validation.

rejected_findings.hypothesis: The lesson should remove the None-vs-zero business distinction because truthiness already handles it.
rejected_findings.reason: That distinction is one of S03's strongest and technically important mental models; Python truthiness deliberately does not encode domain semantics.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: dos registros contienen monto = 0... uno debería contener None
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could overstate None as universal absence.
paragraph_reviews.defense: The paragraph explicitly anchors the meaning to this form/domain contract.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: Puente desde S02... acepta, rechaza o revisión
paragraph_reviews.defense: The sentence restates the only needed prior action: converted values and raw preservation; it does not require safe_int internals.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: truthiness... cero, cadena vacía, lista vacía y None
paragraph_reviews.attack: Introduces list before collections and risks collapsing domain semantics.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Core distinction None vs 0 is explained correctly; list is incidental.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Python llama truthiness a la regla que usa cuando necesita decidir si un valor cuenta como verdadero. Para lo ya conocido: None, False, 0, 0.0 y la cadena vacía son falsy; muchos otros valores son truthy. Eso no expresa la política del negocio: if monto: mezcla 0 con ausencia, mientras if monto is None: pregunta específicamente por ausencia. Las colecciones vacías también son falsy; las estudiarás en S06.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: allowlist... salida temprana... tabla de decisión
paragraph_reviews.attack: Allowlist overgeneralization plus guard clause requires unearned functions.
paragraph_reviews.defense: All three concepts are named with concrete purpose, but function/return dependency is material and safety claim too broad.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Una allowlist es un catálogo explícito de valores admitidos. En un catálogo cerrado, lo no enumerado no se acepta automáticamente: según la política puede ir a review o reject. En S03 aprenderás además a ordenar condiciones y detectar ramas que ya no pueden alcanzarse. Las salidas tempranas con return se introducirán cuando aprendas funciones. Una tabla de decisión enumera combinaciones de condiciones y la acción correspondiente antes de escribir el código.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: un invariante es una promesa que el programa no puede romper
paragraph_reviews.attack: False mental model; raw data can violate a declared invariant.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Intent is to make policy explicit, but wording is technically wrong.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Un invariante es una condición que declaras que debe cumplirse en una etapa concreta del sistema. Por ejemplo: después de validar, un monto aceptado nunca es negativo. Los datos de entrada sí pueden violarla; por eso existen validación y pruebas. Escribe primero la condición y el punto donde debe cumplirse; luego diseña las ramas que detectan sus violaciones.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Result shape depends on future functions/dicts.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: El hilo conductor es una regla que clasifica un campo como accept, reject o review. En S03 mantendremos ese resultado como texto simple para que la atención permanezca en la decisión. Más adelante, cuando aprendas diccionarios, añadiremos code y message como campos estructurados.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: si un campo contiene 0... depende del invariante
paragraph_reviews.attack: Could confuse invariant with current policy due bad definition above.
paragraph_reviews.defense: After F08 repair, prediction prompt is pedagogically strong.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: T1... T4... guard clauses... decision tables
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: T1 trata comparaciones, pertenencia, truthiness y short-circuit. T2 enseña if/elif/else, orden de condiciones y ramas inalcanzables. T3 combina rangos y allowlists y lee una tabla de decisión antes de ver match. T4 formula invariantes, mensajes accionables y casos por rama. Las guard clauses con return se posponen hasta funciones.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: Ritmo orientativo... una pregunta True/False luego una decisión

paragraph_reviews.attack: Internal curriculum ID remains widow term.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Criterio de cierre del proyecto acumulativo CP-N1-A (captura y calidad de datos): cada rama del motor debe ser comprobable con un caso propio, y cada mensaje debe decir qué ocurrió y qué hacer a continuación.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Internal ID unexplained; scope contradicted by code below.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Límites. CASO-LIM-003 es el caso sintético de reglas de esta sección. Trabajas con valores ya convertidos; no construyes lectores CSV/JSON ni dependes de diccionarios/listas todavía. Nunca uses datos personales reales.

Un booleano de negocio puede nacer de ==, !=, <, <=, > o >=. Python también permite encadenar comparaciones: 18 <= edad <= 65 exige que edad cumpla ambas fronteras, y Python evalúa la expresión central una sola vez. En T1-B aprenderás el operador and que permite expresar esa misma condición en dos preguntas.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: in funciona con str, list, set, dict... set ideal
paragraph_reviews.defense: Set receives a microdefinition and membership is a roadmap outcome.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Pertenencia: x in catalogo pregunta si x pertenece al catálogo; x not in catalogo pregunta lo contrario. Para este subtema usaremos un pequeño set literal como {"DNI", "CE"}; piensa en él únicamente como un catálogo sin duplicados. Las diferencias entre listas, sets y diccionarios llegan en S06.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Depends on identity defect from S02.
paragraph_reviews.defense: It repairs the prior model explicitly and is technically correct.
Prediction isolates exactly the taught operators.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: falsy list includes tuples/lists/dicts/set/range and while
paragraph_reviews.defense: Technically accurate list but overbroad for current prerequisite state.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Python usa truthiness cuando una condición necesita decidir si un valor cuenta como verdadero. Entre los valores que ya conoces, None, False, 0, 0.0 y "" son falsy; casi todo valor no vacío/no cero es truthy. Las colecciones vacías siguen la misma idea y las estudiarás en S06.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Definition correct but no skipped-evaluation demonstration.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Operand-return examples are useful but teach a different property.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: and y or hacen short-circuit: evalúan de izquierda a derecha y dejan de evaluar cuando ya conocen qué operando determina el resultado. Por ejemplo, con edad = None, la expresión edad is not None and edad >= 18 devuelve False sin intentar edad >= 18; si intentara esa comparación, fallaría. Además, and/or devuelven uno de sus operandos: "" or "default" produce "default". not siempre produce True o False.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Example relies on a function and loop.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Antes de ejecutar, anota bool(None), bool(0) y bool(-5). Después comprueba cada expresión por separado. Finalmente aplica la política escrita en palabras: None → review; 0 → accept si el contrato lo permite; negativo → reject. No necesitas una función ni un bucle para observar esa diferencia.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: indentation; two if can overwrite status
paragraph_reviews.attack: Overwrite claim not shown in example.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Mechanism is stated concretely and does not require a second example.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Uses function/result language but concept itself clear.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: row of doors; conditions specific above
paragraph_reviews.defense: Qualified with usually and follows first-match model.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Worked code uses function annotations and for.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Boundary prompt is excellent independent of wrapper.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Antes de ejecutar, clasifica 80, 79, 50 y 49 con la cadena if/elif/else mostrada directamente, sin envolverla en una función ni recorrer una lista. Comprueba qué frontera incluye >= y cuál queda para la siguiente rama.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: edad before provided causes exception; guards like access control
paragraph_reviews.defense: Ordering problem is concrete and TypeError prediction is valuable.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Antes de comparar una edad, primero debes decidir qué ocurre si está ausente o tiene un tipo incompatible. Ese orden evita intentar edad < 18 cuando edad es None. En S03 aprenderás a ordenar condiciones; cuando S05 introduzca funciones, ese mismo orden podrá expresarse con guard clauses y return temprano.

paragraph_reviews.defense: Definition is locally clear but not usable by zero-tech learner.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Posponer a S05. En S03 sustituir por: 'Ordena primero las condiciones que detectan casos que no deben avanzar; después evalúa las reglas restantes. El objetivo es que cada caso tenga una ruta clara y que no haya condiciones inalcanzables.'

paragraph_reviews.attack: Depends on isinstance but concept is understandable.
paragraph_reviews.defense: This is a useful validation-order heuristic.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: dead branch x>=0 then elif x>5
funnel guards remove classes and return
paragraph_reviews.defense: Funnel intuition useful but should be expressed as branch ordering until S05.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Piensa en un embudo de condiciones. Primero separas ausentes, luego tipos incompatibles, después valores fuera de rango; cada grupo recibe su decisión y deja de mezclarse con los siguientes. Una rama muerta promete una decisión para la que ya no queda ninguna entrada posible.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Generic allowlist safety claim inherited; set syntax future.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Una allowlist es el catálogo explícito de valores que esta política conoce. Para el ejemplo usaremos un pequeño set literal como {"R-NORTE", "R-SUR"}. Si un valor no aparece, no lo aceptes automáticamente: el contrato debe decir si va a review por desconocido o a reject por política estricta.

paragraph_reviews.defense: Stated as domain policy, not Python law.
Paragraph itself is excellent; issue is T3-B drift.

paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Muestra los dos casos en una tabla simple: R-FUERA,30 → NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST → review; R-COSTA,15 → OUT_OF_RANGE → reject. Conserva esos mismos significados en T3-B.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: decision table forces meaning before syntax
decision table rows condition→action; or dict examples
paragraph_reviews.attack: Promises table but does not show one; dict is future syntax.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Definition is understandable but outcome requires reading an actual table.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Una tabla de decisión se lee fila por fila. Por ejemplo: | code | meaning | status |; OK | regla cumplida | accept; MISSING | dato ausente | review; OUT_OF_RANGE | viola rango | reject; NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST | catálogo no lo reconoce | review; otro | causa desconocida | review. Comprueba primero que todas las situaciones relevantes tienen fila; después traduce cada fila a código.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: match/case literal states, OR patterns, wildcard
paragraph_reviews.defense: Explicitly calls them patterns and scopes to literals; enough for S03.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: prefer if for ranges; You Do dicts
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Prefiere if para rangos y combinaciones de condiciones; usa match cuando una sola variable toma unos pocos estados literales bien definidos. En S03 mantén el resultado como status simple; los resultados estructurados llegarán con diccionarios.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: table first, code later; same policy across dict/if/match
paragraph_reviews.attack: Dict adds future syntax; NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST mapping later drifts.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Tabla primero, código después. Si una fila dice NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST → review, cualquier implementación debe conservar ese resultado hasta que una nueva decisión de negocio cambie explícitamente la tabla.

paragraph_reviews.attack: No actual table exists yet; code uses function/for.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Prediction task becomes strong once a real table is inserted.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Después de leer la tabla visible, predice la fila aplicable a OK, MISSING, OUT_OF_RANGE y FOO. Luego compara dos implementaciones cortas, if/elif y match, sin función wrapper ni bucle, y verifica que ambas respetan exactamente la tabla.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: invariant is promise in Spanish... examples canonical
paragraph_reviews.attack: Needs boundary-scoped definition; current wording partially safer than opening but still treats input expectation as invariant without stage.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Specification vs code distinction is useful.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Un invariante es una condición que debe cumplirse en una etapa declarada. Ejemplo: 'después de validar, contacto es un str de 9 dígitos o queda marcado como review por ausencia'. Escríbelo antes del código y acompáñalo con casos que cumplen y que violan la condición.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: minimum one example per decision state
paragraph_reviews.attack: Insufficient when multiple branches share reject/review.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Mínimo profesional: al menos un ejemplo por rama distinta que tu regla pueda ejecutar. Si dos ramas terminan en reject por causas diferentes, ambas necesitan su propio caso. Comprueba además que todos los estados accept/reject/review que la política promete estén representados.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: counterexamples include blank, short, None, integer
paragraph_reviews.attack: Worked example requires future string methods and containers.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Usa primero un invariante con operaciones ya aprendidas. Ejemplo: 'si edad está presente y se acepta, debe ser int no booleano entre 0 y 120'. Propón None, True, -1, 35 y 121 y clasifica cada caso. Reserva strip/isdigit para la sección de strings.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: Error does not help; explanation + test
field/problem/action; stable codes allow metrics and i18n
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Un mensaje accionable nombra el campo, el problema y la acción esperada. Códigos estables como MISSING u OUT_OF_RANGE permiten contar causas y, más adelante, traducir mensajes sin cambiar la lógica.

paragraph_reviews.current_excerpt: one test per branch; four paths need >=4
paragraph_reviews.defense: This paragraph is the correct rule.
The sequence is self-explaining enough and T4 is explicitly verification.

paragraph_reviews.attack: Relies on dict structure before S06 and policy code drift.
paragraph_reviews.defense: Conceptual separation is useful but container should not be prerequisite.
paragraph_reviews.improved_version: Separa tres ideas aunque todavía no las empaquetes en un diccionario: status guía la decisión, code nombra la causa de forma estable y message orienta a una persona. Conserva la misma relación causa→status en toda la sección.

Top-level comparisons are good; set needs a one-sentence preview but no future loop/function syntax.
Correct policy but function/loop wrappers are future; short-circuit skipping is not demonstrated.
if/elif logic is good but function annotation/return and for loop obscure first exposure.

Unknown-vs-range policy is useful, but later mapping must remain consistent.
match syntax itself is adequate, but NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST switches to reject and wrappers use future syntax.
Too many future concepts for invariant first exposure.
Branch-testing idea is good, but bool is accepted as int and containers/loops/functions remain premature.

Core contract drift: invariant definition, NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST status and branch-coverage minimum are internally inconsistent.
Worked examples often demonstrate surrounding syntax rather than isolating the new control-flow concept for a true novice.
